pathway.title: Magnera Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is moderate on the issuer's measure and high on the reported one. Total debt is 5.11x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million, down from 5.51x at the fiscal 2025 year end, and 7.60x trailing reported EBITDA of USD 250 million. The USD 122 million gap between them is restructuring, optimisation and non-cash add-backs, so the adjusted multiple is credible only if those charges stop recurring. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04

- Interest cover and cash conversion are the weakest dimensions. Net cash interest of USD 124 million took 35.03% of fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA, with reported cover at 1.70x, and free cash flow after capital spending was USD 113 million over the trailing twelve months against adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million. Little cash is therefore left for debt reduction, so deleveraging depends on earnings growth more than on repayment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C05; calculation C06

- Near-term liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest support. Cash of USD 280 million plus an undrawn USD 350 million revolver gives USD 630 million, equal to 33.14% of debt, no debt matures before October 2029, and the term loan and secured notes have no financial maintenance covenants. Default before 2029 would need a sharp earnings fall, but availability under the revolver is not measured and 58% of cash is outside the U.S. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C07

- The earnings base is improving, partly through self-help and with concentrated customers. Adjusted EBITDA rose 8.79% in the third quarter on a USD 11 million price-cost gain, and trailing adjusted EBITDA is USD 18 million above fiscal 2025, but restructuring charges were USD 61 million in nine months and the top ten customers hold about 42% of sales without long-term arrangements. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C08

- Control weaknesses and undisclosed ownership limit confidence in the figures. Internal control over financial reporting was not effective at the fiscal 2025 year end and disclosure controls were not effective at June 27, 2026, and no current holder is named. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium, which widens the margin of error around every metric above. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Refinancing risk is back-ended but concentrated. USD 500 million falls due in 2029 and USD 1,466 million in 2031, 74.57% of principal in the later year, and the book value of marketable debt exceeded fair value by USD 48 million at June 27, 2026, down from USD 136 million at March 28, 2026. The narrowing gap suggests debt is trading better, yet repayment slowed to USD 2 million in the third quarter, so the 2031 maturity will need market access rather than internal cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-03-28_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C09; calculation C10

- Overall the business profile is average and the cash-flow profile weak. The top risk is a raw-material cost spike or customer loss that cuts adjusted EBITDA toward the lowest recent quarterly run-rate of USD 336 million, which would lift debt to 5.66x and cash interest to 36.90% of earnings before any liquidity stress. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11

runs.text: Strengths. First, there is no debt maturity before October 2029 and no financial maintenance covenant on the term loan and secured notes, so default before 2029 would need a sharp earnings fall rather than a covenant trip. Second, liquidity of USD 630 million, cash plus the undrawn revolver, equals 33.14% of debt and is the main cushion against a near-term cash shortfall. Third, deleveraging is under way: debt repayments of USD 65 million and trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 372 million lowered adjusted leverage from 5.51x to 5.11x. Fourth, the business spans two regions, 45 plants and more than 1,000 customers, so no single plant or region carries the whole credit. Fifth, the price-cost spread turned positive by USD 11 million in the third quarter, showing that pass-through can work. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C07

Weaknesses. First, net cash interest of USD 124 million took 35.03% of fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA and reported cover was 1.70x, so a small earnings fall removes cover. Second, free cash flow is thin: USD 32 million in nine months against an outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million, with a third-quarter outflow of USD 28 million. Third, the gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA is USD 122 million, 32.80% of adjusted earnings, so leverage is 7.60x if add-backs are not credited. Fourth, the top ten customers hold about 42% of sales and many have no long-term arrangement, while resin and pulp costs pass through only with a lag. Fifth, internal controls are not effective and ownership is not disclosed. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C12

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On November 4, 2024 Treasure Holdco, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Berry Global Group, Inc., merged with Glatfelter Corporation, which was renamed Magnera Corporation. Treasure shareholders received 90% of the combined company and Glatfelter shareholders kept 10%, and Treasure was the accounting acquirer, so the fiscal 2024 figures are carve-out statements of the business Berry contributed. Total consideration was the USD 74 million fair value of Glatfelter common stock, and Glatfelter debt with a fair value of USD 869 million was assumed. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 32

To fund the closing the company put in place a USD 785 million term loan due 2031, a USD 800 million issue of 7.25% First Priority Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and a USD 350 million asset-based revolver due 2029, and it kept Glatfelter's 4.75% notes due 2029. The statement of cash flows shows proceeds from long-term borrowings of USD 1,556 million, a cash distribution to Berry of USD 1,111 million and repayments of USD 484 million; the filing says the term loan and 7.25% note proceeds retired part of Glatfelter's debt and funded the distribution. The face amounts of USD 785 million and USD 800 million add to USD 1,585 million, USD 29 million more than the cash proceeds shown, and no source explains the difference. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C01

The fiscal 2026 cash flow statements show no proceeds from borrowings. Outstanding principal has been reduced by prepayments, to USD 706 million on the term loan and USD 760 million on the 7.25% notes at June 27, 2026, while the revolver is undrawn. No acquisition, sponsor transaction or refinancing after the merger is described, and the third-quarter report says only that the company intends to pursue acquisition targets. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.value: Financial foundation for Magnera Corp (issuer magn) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the fiscal 2025 annual statements, the three fiscal 2026 quarterly statements, carrying-value debt, liquidity, trailing twelve-month leverage and coverage, and separately identified subsequent events.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnera is thinly covered but slowly deleveraging: debt is 5.11x trailing adjusted EBITDA at June 27, 2026 against 5.51x at the fiscal 2025 year end, yet 7.60x on reported EBITDA, so creditors should underwrite on cash generation, not on adjusted earnings. Net debt fell by only USD 26 million over three quarters, from USD 1,647 million to USD 1,621 million, while nine-month free cash flow was only USD 32 million.

fields.value: Leverage is falling because debt is being repaid, not because earnings are rising fast. Principal fell by USD 65 million between the fiscal 2025 year end and June 27, 2026, equal to the nine-month repayments, while trailing adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 354 million to USD 372 million. The same debt is 7.60x trailing reported EBITDA of USD 250 million, because USD 122 million of add-backs separate reported from adjusted EBITDA, namely restructuring, business optimization and other charges and non-cash items that the issuer does not count as ongoing operations. If those charges persist, the adjusted multiple overstates debt capacity and creditors are closer to the reported multiple.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage is the thinnest point of the credit. Net interest expense was USD 112 million over nine months against adjusted EBITDA of USD 282 million, and the only reported cash interest figure, USD 124 million for fiscal 2025, gives adjusted cover of 2.85x and reported cover of 1.70x. The floating-rate term loan prices at 4.25% over SOFR, so a 0.25% rate move changes annual interest by about USD 2 million; interim cash interest is not disclosed, so interim cover is not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow quality is weak relative to the earnings reported. Fiscal 2025 operating cash flow of USD 103 million less capital expenditure of USD 67 million is USD 36 million, not the USD 126 million the issuer prints, because the issuer adds USD 90 million of pre-merger cash flow. In the nine months to June 2026 operating cash flow was USD 76 million and free cash flow USD 32 million, and the third quarter alone used USD 13 million of operating cash, so the outlook of USD 90 million to USD 110 million for the year depends on a fourth quarter of USD 58 million to USD 78 million. The issuer lowered its operating cash flow outlook to USD 150 million to USD 170 million while keeping the free cash flow range by cutting planned capital spending to USD 60 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is cash of USD 280 million, about 58% of it outside the U.S., plus an undrawn USD 350 million asset-based revolver due November 2029, more than twelve months away. Availability under that revolver depends on a borrowing base and letters of credit that are not disclosed, so undrawn capacity is a ceiling, not a measure, and no debt matures before 2029. The term loan and secured notes carry no financial maintenance covenants, only negative covenants, and the revolver's covenants are not described, so covenant headroom is not established. The refinancing risk is therefore later and larger: USD 500 million in 2029 and USD 1,466 million in 2031 on a business that generated USD 32 million of free cash flow in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Magnera Corp (issuer magn) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, the November 2024 merger and financing, ownership and control, operating drivers, capital allocation and governance, from the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnera's creditor risk is a debt-funded separation and weak controls, not a sponsor: no controlling holder is disclosed, but USD 1,111 million went to the former parent at closing and internal controls are not effective.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is diversified by region and end market but concentrated by customer, with the top ten customers about 42% of net sales, and its thin segment margins depend on passing resin and pulp costs through to customers with a lag; the latest year shows self-help gains but also USD 61 million of restructuring cost in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership and control are undisclosed rather than benign. The 10-K says the pre-merger Treasure shareholders received 90% of the combined company and the Glatfelter shareholders kept 10%, but names no holder, board seat, consent right or fee, because those items sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. There is no sponsor in the run settings, so the creditor question is whether any holder can steer financial policy, and the documents read cannot answer it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The capital structure was built for the separation, not for the operating business. The new term loan and the 7.25% secured notes raised USD 1,556 million of cash proceeds, USD 1,111 million of which went to the former parent as a cash distribution (71.40% of the proceeds), and the filing says the remainder helped retire part of Glatfelter's debt. Creditors therefore carry interest on borrowing whose main use was a payment to a holder that no longer controls the company.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration and the lag in cost pass-through are the main business risks. The top customer is about 14% and the top ten customers about 42% of net sales, many customers have no long-term arrangement, and resin and pulp costs are passed on only over time. In fiscal 2025 organic volume fell by 2% and the price-cost spread cost the Americas segment USD 14 million of Adjusted EBITDA, so a raw-material spike or a customer switch hits earnings before prices catch up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margins are improving through self-help that costs cash. Restructuring and other activities charges were USD 89 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 61 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, equal to 25.14% and 21.63% of Adjusted EBITDA, while the third-quarter price-cost spread added USD 11 million. The synergies the issuer cites are management estimates, so creditors should treat them as unrealised until cash flow shows them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-09-27_form10k.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-27_form10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_ef20079553_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance is the clearest creditor-adverse area. Internal control over financial reporting was not effective at the fiscal 2025 year end, the auditor gave an adverse opinion on it, disclosure controls were still not effective at June 27, 2026, and legacy U.S. systems run under a transition services agreement with the former parent. Management reports no material error, so the effect is lower confidence in the numbers and slower detection of problems, not a known misstatement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation since closing has favoured creditors, but the stated appetite for acquisitions could reverse that. The cash flow statements show debt repayments of USD 65 million in nine months and no dividend or buyback line, while the third-quarter report says the company intends to pursue further acquisitions. A debt-funded purchase would raise leverage that is only slowly falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sponsor and governance risk is Medium. Documented behaviour is mixed, the control environment is weak and ownership is not disclosed, but there is no recorded dividend recapitalisation, creditor-adverse amendment or exchange since closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that behaviour since closing has been creditor-friendly: the company repaid USD 65 million of debt in nine months, shows no distribution after the closing payment, described the third quarter as a record with Adjusted EBITDA of USD 99 million and kept its free cash flow outlook. The auditor's opinion on the financial statements themselves was unqualified and the largest customer is only about 14% of sales. The view would turn more positive if remediation removed the control weaknesses and the proxy statement showed dispersed holders with no fee arrangements. It would turn more negative if a holder with consent rights emerged, if an acquisition were funded with debt, or if debt repayment stopped while restructuring spend continued.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so the finding that no controlling holder is disclosed could change if a holder with board or consent rights exists; sponsor-style risks would then apply.

fields.name: Quote

fields.value: On November 4, 2024 Treasure Holdco, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Berry Global Group, Inc., merged with Glatfelter Corporation, which was renamed Magnera Corporation. Treasure shareholders received 90% of the combined company and Glatfelter shareholders kept 10%, and Treasure was the accounting acquirer, so the fiscal 2024 figures are carve-out statements of the business Berry contributed. Total consideration was the USD 74 million fair value of Glatfelter common stock, and Glatfelter debt with a fair value of USD 869 million was assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: To fund the closing the company put in place a USD 785 million term loan due 2031, a USD 800 million issue of 7.25% First Priority Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and a USD 350 million asset-based revolver due 2029, and it kept Glatfelter's 4.75% notes due 2029. The statement of cash flows shows proceeds from long-term borrowings of USD 1,556 million, a cash distribution to Berry of USD 1,111 million and repayments of USD 484 million; the filing says the term loan and 7.25% note proceeds retired part of Glatfelter's debt and funded the distribution. The face amounts of USD 785 million and USD 800 million add to USD 1,585 million, USD 29 million more than the cash proceeds shown, and no source explains the difference.

Pricing power is limited: costs pass through contractually only over time, at renewals and by other means, and customers can switch suppliers. Buyer power is high because the top ten customers hold about 42% of sales and many have no long-term arrangement, so volume and price are renegotiated at renewal and earnings can step down. Supplier power is moderate to high because resin and pulp prices are set outside the company and pass through with a lag, which makes cash conversion volatile. The threat of new entrants is moderate because plants, technology and customer qualification need capital, and the threat of substitutes is not established by the documents read.

fields.value: The scenario starts with a raw-material cost spike that is passed on late while European volume stays soft, as in fiscal 2025 when organic volume fell 2% and the Americas price-cost spread cost USD 14 million. The first operating break is a negative price-cost spread, which cuts adjusted EBITDA; an illustrative case uses the lowest reported quarter, USD 84 million, annualised to USD 336 million, USD 36 million or 9.68% below the trailing figure; that quarter included Glatfelter only from November 4, 2024, so the case is harsher than a like-for-like trough. Debt of USD 1,901 million would be 5.66x that EBITDA and cash interest of USD 124 million would take 36.90% of it, and free cash flow would fall from USD 113 million to about USD 77 million before any tax effect. Management levers are cutting capital spending, which already fell by USD 20 million, ending restructuring spend and stopping prepayments; liquidity of USD 630 million and the absence of maturities before 2029 mean resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis in the window, but refinancing the 2029 notes at that earnings level would be harder and costlier. The observable triggers are a negative price-cost spread, organic volume turning negative again and a fourth-quarter free cash flow below USD 58 million.

fields.value: Overall, Magnera presents an average business profile supported by regional and end-market diversification, 45 plants and no debt maturity before 2029, but credit quality is constrained by thin cash cover, the USD 122 million gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA, customer concentration and a weak control environment. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was USD 32 million in nine months and negative in the third quarter. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth and market access for USD 1,966 million of principal due in 2029 and 2031. The primary downside path is a raw-material cost spike passed on late, cutting adjusted EBITDA toward the lowest quarterly run-rate. Further analysis would require revolver availability, interim cash interest, receivable-program balances, the proxy statement and the executed debt documents. Top risk: thin cash cover on a debt load that must be refinanced in 2029 and 2031.
